prompt: Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with whiplash after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 8 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1009; do not mention it.)
text:
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache beginning the day of the incident. Examination revealed restricted cervical range of motion, particularly in extension and rotation, with paraspinal muscle tenderness and mild muscle guarding. Neurological screening was within normal limits, with no focal motor or sensory deficits and symmetric deep tendon reflexes. Cervical radiographs were obtained and showed no acute fracture or subluxation.

Over eight visits, treatment consisted of a combination of manual therapy, soft tissue mobilization, progressive cervical range-of-motion exercises, and postural education. Modalities including heat and ultrasound were used for symptom relief during the early phase of care. Headache frequency decreased steadily as neck mobility improved.

At the most recent visit, the patient reported pain reduced by approximately two-thirds from initial presentation, with near-full cervical range of motion and only intermittent stiffness after prolonged sitting. Functional limitations at work and during daily activities had largely resolved. The patient was advised to continue a home exercise program and to return if symptoms worsen or new neurological symptoms develop. Prognosis for full recovery is good.
